intro: Lesson 32: Weekly progress check and Micro-DIRT (Act 1 scenes 1 to 3). Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Micro-DIRT: one precise change
points: Add a Zoom in on one word
Turn a plot point into a concept
Embed the quotation in your sentence
Replace a vague verb with 'suggests' or 'conveys'

questions.q: Retrieval and vocabulary check (portal): ten questions on Act 1 and the week's vocabulary.
questions.a: See the answer slide: 1606; James I; regicide; 'Fair is foul'; Cawdor; Captain; hamartia; tunnel vision; context; roadmap.

questions.q: Unseen paragraph: explain one method the writer uses (pupil PDF).
questions.a: One method with evidence and effect.

questions.q: Core: Micro-DIRT in the portal response box. Improve your Week 1 introduction or paragraph with one precise change. Starter: 'Shakespeare presents...'
questions.a: An improved paragraph with the chosen change clearly made.

questions.q: Extend: write a target for Week 2.
Stretch: write one sentence predicting how Macbeth will respond to the prophecies.
questions.a: For example: Macbeth will be tempted, because the prophecy speaks to an ambition already in him.

questions.q: Which change makes the biggest difference?
options: Turning 'Macbeth is brave' into an argument about heroism and its fall
questions.a: B) Turning 'Macbeth is brave' into an argument about heroism and its fall. Conceptual change adds marks; the others are cosmetic.

questions.q: Answer the ponder in one sentence.
questions.a: A precise change, e.g. adding a Zoom in.
